passages.scripture: Brothers, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for the Israelites is for their salvation.

lines.text: Paul is speaking to his fellow believers.
Paul cares deeply for the Israelites.
Paul wants the Israelites to be saved.
Paul prays to God for the salvation of the Israelites.
Paul’s heart desires their salvation.

passages.scripture: For I testify about them that they are zealous for God, but not on the basis of knowledge.

lines.text: Paul testifies about the Israelites.
The Israelites have zeal for God.
Their zeal is strong.
But the zeal of the Israelites is not based on knowledge.
The Israelites do not understand correctly.

passages.scripture: Because they were ignorant of God’s righteousness and sought to establish their own, they did not submit to God’s righteousness.

lines.text: The Israelites did not know God’s righteousness.
The Israelites were ignorant of the righteousness of God.
The Israelites tried to make their own righteousness.
The Israelites did not submit to God’s righteousness.

passages.scripture: For Christ is the end of the law, to bring righteousness to everyone who believes.

lines.text: Christ is the end of the law.
Christ brings righteousness.
Christ gives righteousness to everyone who believes in Him.

passages.scripture: For concerning the righteousness that is by the law, Moses writes: “The man who does these things will live by them.”

lines.text: Moses was a leader of Israel and a prophet of God.
Moses wrote about righteousness that comes from the law.
The person who does these things written in the law will live by them.
Anyone who follows the law will have life and blessings through their obedience to the law.

passages.scripture: But the righteousness that is by faith says: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ (that is, to bring Christ down) or, ‘Who will descend into the Abyss?’ (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).”

lines.text: Do not say in your heart, “Who will go up into heaven?”
This means, do not try to bring Christ down from heaven.
Do not say in your heart, “Who will go down into the Abyss?”
This means, do not try to bring Christ up from the dead.
The righteousness that comes by faith speaks in this way.

passages.scripture: But what does it say? “The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart,” that is, the word of faith we are proclaiming: that if you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.

lines.text: What does the righteousness that is by faith say?
The word is near you.
The word is in your mouth.
The word is in your heart.
This word is the message of faith.
Paul proclaims this message of faith.
Jesus is Lord.
We must confess with our mouths that Jesus is Lord.
God raised Jesus from the dead.
We must believe in our hearts that God raised Jesus from the dead.
If we do this, then we will be saved.
God will save us.

passages.scripture: For with your heart you believe and are justified, and with your mouth you confess and are saved.

lines.text: We believe in Jesus with our hearts.
Through our faith, God justifies us.
We confess Jesus with our mouths.
Our confession leads to our salvation.

passages.scripture: It is just as the Scripture says: “Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”

lines.text: Anyone who believes in Jesus will not be put to shame.
This promise applies to every believer in Him.
The Scripture says this about Jesus Christ.

passages.scripture: For there is no difference between Jew and Greek: The same Lord is Lord of all, and gives richly to all who call on Him, for, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”

lines.text: God does not see a difference between Jews and those who are not Jews, such as Greeks.
God is the same Lord for everyone.
God is Lord over all people.
God saves everyone who calls on Him.
Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.

passages.scripture: How then can they call on the One in whom they have not believed? And how can they believe in the One of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone to preach?

lines.text: A preacher preaches the word of the Lord.
People hear the preacher preaching the word of the Lord and believe.
People believe the word of the Lord and so they call upon the Lord.
People call upon the Lord and are saved.
People first believe in the Lord and then call on the Lord.
People first hear the word of the Lord to believe in the Lord.
A preacher first preaches the word of the Lord for people to hear the word.

passages.scripture: And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”

lines.text: A preacher must be sent before he can preach.
God sends preachers to share the word of God.
Some people bring good news.
Their feet are beautiful.
Scripture says this in Isaiah about those who bring good news.

passages.scripture: But not all of them welcomed the good news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”

lines.text: The good news was preached, but not all people accepted the message.
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah spoke to God.
Isaiah said, “Lord, who has believed our message?”

passages.scripture: Consequently, faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.

lines.text: Faith comes from hearing.
Hearing comes through the word of Christ.

passages.scripture: But I ask, did they not hear? Indeed they did: “Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.”

lines.text: Paul asks if the people of Israel didn't hear the word of God.
Paul answers his own question saying, yes, they did hear.
The voices of those speaking the word of God have gone out into all the earth.
The word of God has gone to the ends of the world.

passages.scripture: I ask instead, did Israel not understand? First, Moses says: “I will make you jealous by those who are not a nation; I will make you angry by a nation without understanding.”

lines.text: Paul asks if Israel heard the word of God, but did not understand the word.
Paul answers his own question, and the first answer to his question are words from Moses in Deuteronomy.
Moses speaks God's words.
God says God will make Israel jealous by those who are not a nation.
God says God will make Israel angry by a nation without understanding.
God uses other nations to make Israel jealous and angry.
These other nations do not have understanding.
These other nations are not truly a nation.
God does this to teach Israel.

passages.scripture: And Isaiah boldly says: “I was found by those who did not seek Me; I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me.”

lines.text: Isaiah was a prophet of God.
Isaiah spoke with boldness.
God said people who did not seek God found God.
God said God revealed Himself to people who did not ask for Him.
Isaiah said these words from God.

passages.scripture: But as for Israel he says: “All day long I have held out My hands to a disobedient and obstinate people.”

lines.text: God speaks about Israel.
God has held out His hands to Israel.
God has held out His hands all day long.
However, Israel has been a disobedient people.
Israel has been an obstinate people.
